entry.title: The Role of a Software Architect – And Why It Often Can't Be Fulfilled
entry.summary: In many organizations, the title "Software Architect" exists. It is often used to signal technical maturity — both internally and externally. But maturity doesn't come from naming. It comes from the organizational anchoring of the function. Architecture is a design function. It requires context, influence, time, and a clear mandate. If any of these is missing, architecture doesn't emerge — instead, what emerges is the sum of local decisions that no one holds together. The question is therefore not: "Do we have an architect?"
